method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA) 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy' (content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition)). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © ASCIA 2026; no reuse terms stated (read at the page footer ('© ASCIA 2026, Content updated June 2026')). The source's words are NOT reproduced here.

claims.claim: **Breastfeeding comes first** because of its benefits for mother and baby; this guidance is for when it is not possible.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A breastfeeding mother does not necessarily need to cut out cow's milk.** Discuss it with a medical specialist, and have a dietitian supervise any exclusion.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Eczema on its own does not justify a specialised infant formula.**
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: 🚩 **Do not use these for CMA:** partially hydrolysed or A2 formula, any standard formula (anti-reflux, lactose-free, organic, newborn or follow-on types included), or goat and other animal milks. Unlisted plant or vegan formulas lack hypoallergenicity and growth data.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Rice-protein formula is an option unless the child is allergic to rice,** but evidence for it in non-IgE food allergy is limited. Of the two in Australia, only Novalac Allergy has product-specific hypoallergenicity and growth studies; Alula Allergy is batch-tested for milk and soy contamination.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Use amino acid formula (AAF) or extensively hydrolysed formula (eHF) when growth is poor or there are several non-IgE food allergies.**
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If the usual formula is unavailable, swap within the same group** (one eHF for another eHF), after reviewing why it was first chosen and any change in history.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **A thriving child over 6 months** whose earlier reaction to cow's milk formula was mild or moderate, and who was put on eHF before 6 months, can be switched to soy formula.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **If AAF for over-12-month-olds is needed but unavailable, involve a paediatric allergy dietitian** to adapt a substitute recipe. With any formula change, go over the mixing instructions with the family, since scoop-to-water ratios differ a lot.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Over 12 months on soy formula:** calcium-fortified soy milk can take its place, provided growth is good and the child eats a broad range of family foods.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Allergic to both cow's milk and soy:** most plant milks without calcium fortification (such as rice or soy milk) have too little protein, fat and calcium for young children unless growth and nutrition are carefully checked.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Up to four years of age, 400-500 mL a day of calcium-fortified plant milk meets calcium needs;** drinking more can blunt appetite, intake and growth.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23

claims.claim: **Every infant or child with CMA should see a paediatric allergy dietitian** for a nutrition assessment.
claims.locator: Australasian Society of Clinical Immunology and Allergy (ASCIA), 'ASCIA Information for Health Professionals: Milk Substitutes in Cow's Milk Allergy', content updated June 2026 (supersedes the December 2025 edition), https://www.allergy.org.au/hp/papers/guide-for-milk-substitutes-cows-milk-allergy, retrieved 2026-09-23
